title: Productive staple farming with seawater and a closed salt balance

concept.text: Proposed innovation: a farming system that produces nutritionally significant staple food using seawater as its principal irrigation source while maintaining sustainable water and salt balances over time. The advance combines a productive salt-tolerant crop with agronomy, irrigation, drainage and environmental protection. A plant's ability to survive salty water would address only one part of the goal.

Conceptual clarification: a closed salt balance means accounting for incoming salt, its storage within the system and its eventual removal or containment. It does not mean assuming that salt disappears or that every material stream must circulate indefinitely. The system would need to explain where salt goes and how its management protects the productive growing environment, groundwater and neighboring ecosystems.

significance.text: Conditional significance: if staple crops could achieve useful yields and acceptable costs under these conditions, suitable coastal and arid locations could produce food with substantially less freshwater irrigation. The revolutionary capability would be the combination of food productivity, seawater use and durable environmental performance, rather than salt tolerance considered alone.

Conditional downstream possibilities include additional agricultural production and reduced competition for freshwater. Their scale would depend on suitable land, seawater conveyance, energy, drainage infrastructure, salt disposal or containment, economics and ecological constraints. Seawater use alone would not establish net freshwater savings: freshwater used for crop establishment, dilution, flushing or other operations would also need to be counted. The proposal therefore does not imply that all coastal land becomes farmland or that regional water scarcity would automatically be resolved.

missing_breakthrough.text: Target capability: integrate staple-food productivity at seawater-level salinity with a farm system that manages incoming salt for multiple growing seasons. The supplied evidence does not establish whether this complete capability remains absent from the field. It does, however, define a coherent target whose crop, engineering and environmental requirements must be demonstrated together.

Proposed engineering and scientific questions include whether a candidate crop can maintain harvestable yield and nutritional value throughout its life cycle under the intended irrigation conditions; how the growing environment remains productive as salt enters; and how drainage, salt removal or containment can operate at acceptable cost. Crop survival, a single successful harvest and sustainable staple production are different levels of accomplishment.

System-level synthesis: moving salt away from the crop would not by itself settle the environmental problem. A convincing design must identify the destination and consequences of salt-bearing drainage or other exported material, including effects beyond the farm boundary. These are requirements of the proposed system; the supplied retained scientific material does not independently establish their quantitative severity or the best technical solution.

current_state.text: The supplied research reports seawater-irrigated salt-tolerant crops and experimental plants, but the validated review could not verify those demonstrations from the retained material. No usable field-trial text, measured crop yields, seawater fractions, production costs or multi-year salt balances were supplied. Existing partial achievements and the availability of a competitive staple-food system therefore remain unresolved in this record. This evidence gap does not show that the reported demonstrations are false or that the proposed system is impossible.

The research identifies a paper attributed to Josefin Thorslund, Marc F. P. Bierkens and colleagues, titled “Common irrigation drivers of freshwater salinisation in river basins worldwide,” dated 9 July 2021, and describes findings from seven river basins. However, the validated review reports that the retained PubMed copy contains only a cookie-access message, with no abstract, results or bibliographic text confirming the paper's identity. Consequently, the date, seven-basin scope and reported irrigation-related findings are supplied research metadata, not verified scientific findings in this record. The earlier description of an abstract-only assessment must be corrected to an access-limited assessment with no scientific text available.

The research also reports finding a potentially relevant seawater-irrigated halophyte field-trial paper whose publisher page returned an access error. The review received neither retained field-trial text nor a record documenting that access attempt. Its methods and results cannot therefore be used to establish an achievement here. Even if the reported river-basin study were verified, evidence about irrigation-related freshwater salinisation would inform a management constraint; it would not by itself establish the feasibility or impossibility of seawater staple farming.

No bounded freshness search record was supplied to establish the field's status as of 1 November 2026. The source index records a retrieval on 11 November 2026, but a retrieval date does not establish the recency or completeness of scientific coverage. The supplied materials consequently support neither a claim that the full innovation has been achieved nor a definitive claim that it remains unachieved.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: operate a farm-scale system for several years that produces a nutritionally significant staple crop using predominantly seawater, with yields and costs competitive against explicitly identified local alternatives. Before testing, define the seawater share, irrigation salinity, production area, duration, nutritional contribution and economic comparison. These are proposed evaluation criteria, not established consensus thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed accounting and environmental demonstration: publish complete water and salt balances covering inputs, outputs and changes in storage. Include freshwater used at every production stage, salt retained in the growing environment, salt exported in harvested material or drainage, and the destination of managed waste streams. Show that productive growing conditions persist and that groundwater and neighboring ecosystems meet predefined, site-appropriate protection criteria. Explain measurement uncertainty and any material balance that remains unclosed.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed accounting and environmental demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: make methods, measurements and cost assumptions available for independent assessment and replication. Test enough seasons and locations to characterize performance under the conditions claimed, and report failures and operating limits alongside successful trials. Results should specify crop, climate, soil or growing medium, seawater composition, infrastructure and energy requirements. Finite trials would establish demonstrated breadth within those conditions, not literal universality across staple crops or farming environments.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: AGR-01, “Cereal crops supplied predominantly by biological nitrogen fixation,” and AGR-02, “A transferable carbon-concentrating system for C3 staple crops,” address different crop capabilities that could potentially complement seawater farming. Biological nitrogen supply concerns crop nutrition; carbon concentration concerns photosynthetic performance. Neither title implies seawater tolerance or a sustainable farm salt balance.

Roster-based synthesis: AGR-03, “Reliable clonal seed reproduction across major hybrid crops,” concerns reproduction and the preservation of hybrid combinations. AGR-04, “High-yield perennial versions of the major grain-crop portfolio,” concerns productive perennial growth. Either capability might be combined with a suitable seawater crop, but neither establishes productivity under seawater irrigation or resolves salt management over time.

Roster-based synthesis: AGR-06, “Rapidly programmable, durable crop immunity,” addresses disease resistance, while AGR-07, “A general, rapid method for creating productive crops from wild plants,” could offer a route for developing productive crops from salt-tolerant wild candidates. That possible connection does not make the concepts equivalent: seawater staple farming could use several crop-development approaches, and any candidate would still require agronomic, nutritional, economic and salt-balance validation.

Roster-based synthesis: AGR-08, “Economically accessible, end-to-end autonomous field farming,” could overlap through automated irrigation, monitoring and drainage operations, but autonomy does not establish seawater compatibility or environmental performance. AGR-09, “Food crops that reliably build durable, additional soil carbon,” shares an interest in long-term growing conditions and environmental outcomes, but durable additional carbon storage and sustainable salt management are separate achievements requiring separate evidence.

change_log.change: Preserved AGR-05's identity and expanded the explanation of the combined crop-and-farming system.
change_log.reason: The innovation requires staple productivity and sustained salt management together; evidence limitations do not justify removing the concept.

change_log.change: Clarified closed salt balance as explicit accounting, storage management and responsible removal or containment.
change_log.reason: This preserves the original system requirement without implying that salt disappears or that indefinite internal recirculation is required.

change_log.change: Replaced the earlier abstract-only characterization with the review's finding that the retained copy contains a cookie-access message and no scientific text.
change_log.reason: The available artifact cannot substantiate the paper's identity, abstract or findings.

change_log.change: Retained the reported 2021 date and seven-basin scope only as unverified supplied research metadata.
change_log.reason: The quantitative and bibliographic details remain potentially useful, but the retained artifact does not verify them.

change_log.change: Qualified reported crop demonstrations, the field-trial access failure and claims about the full capability remaining missing.
change_log.reason: No usable demonstration text, documented field-trial access attempt or bounded freshness search was supplied; lack of verification is not evidence of falsity.

change_log.change: Integrated conditional freshwater savings, deployment constraints and the distinction between salinisation evidence and feasibility evidence.
change_log.reason: These distinctions preserve the proposed impact while preventing regional benefits or impossibility claims from being inferred without support.

change_log.change: Expanded proposed completion criteria to include measurable definitions, complete accounting, independent replication and explicit operating boundaries.
change_log.reason: The review identified the need to operationalize seawater share, competitive performance and environmental protection without presenting proposed thresholds as established standards.

change_log.change: Explained overlap and distinctions with every other supplied roster entry.
change_log.reason: Related agricultural capabilities may complement AGR-05 but do not replace its seawater productivity and salt-management requirements.

unresolved_issues: The retained PubMed artifact does not verify the claimed paper's identity, publication date, seven-basin scope or scientific findings.
The crop demonstrations and potentially relevant halophyte field trial lack supplied scientific text sufficient to assess species, salinity, yield, nutrition, duration, economics or salt management.
The reported publisher access failure has no supplied retained artifact or search record documenting it.
The absence of a bounded freshness search leaves the availability of a complete system unresolved as of 1 November 2026; the later retrieval timestamp does not resolve this.
Operational definitions remain to be set for predominantly seawater, farm scale, nutritionally significant production, competitive yield and cost, and acceptable environmental performance.
No supplied measurements establish net freshwater savings, long-term salt storage, drainage impacts or the cost and environmental consequences of salt removal or containment.
